questions.q: What is a flowchart used to show?
questions.a: A process, sequence or cycle of steps in order.
Nitrogen cycle / carbon cycle / water cycle.

steps.label: Fatty deposits
steps.note: Cholesterol and other fatty substances build up slowly inside the walls of the coronary arteries over many years.

steps.label: Artery narrows
steps.note: The build-up forms a hard plaque that makes the lumen of the artery narrower, so less blood can flow through it.

steps.label: Reduced blood flow
steps.note: The narrowed artery delivers less oxygenated blood to the heart muscle, especially during exercise when demand is high.

steps.label: Chest pain (angina)
steps.note: The oxygen-starved heart muscle causes a tight, painful, crushing feeling in the chest known as angina.

steps.label: Clot forms
steps.note: A plaque can rupture and trigger a blood clot that suddenly blocks the artery completely.

steps.label: Heart attack
steps.note: With no blood supply, part of the heart muscle dies — this is a myocardial infarction, or heart attack.

steps.label: Light absorbed
steps.note: Chlorophyll in the chloroplasts absorbs light energy from the Sun to power the reaction.

steps.label: Glucose made
steps.note: Carbon dioxide and water are combined into glucose, storing the light energy as chemical energy.

steps.label: Energy released
steps.note: Respiration in the mitochondria breaks glucose back down to release usable energy for the cell.

nodes.label: Plant proteins
nodes.note: Absorbed and built into amino acids

nodes.label: Decay
nodes.note: Decomposers return nitrogen to the soil

developing.q: Name the first stage in the development of coronary heart disease.
developing.a: Fatty deposits build up in the coronary artery walls.

developing.q: State what a flowchart arrow represents.
developing.a: The direction of the process from one step to the next.

reaching.q: Explain why a narrowed coronary artery can cause a heart attack.
reaching.a: Less oxygenated blood reaches the heart muscle; a clot can block it completely, so muscle cells die.

mastering.q: Describe the full sequence from fatty deposits to a heart attack, explaining each stage.
mastering.a: Fatty deposits narrow the artery, reducing blood flow, causing angina; a ruptured plaque forms a clot that blocks the artery, killing heart muscle in a heart attack.

developing.q: What builds up inside the coronary arteries in CHD?

reaching.q: Why does a narrowed artery cause angina?
reaching.a: Less oxygenated blood reaches the heart muscle, causing chest pain.

mastering.q: Explain the whole CHD sequence to a heart attack.
mastering.a: Deposits narrow the artery, blood flow drops, a clot blocks it, and heart muscle dies.
